verdict.rationale: Unity ships an official in-editor 'AI Assistant' package (com.unity.ai.assistant) documented to create assets, automate workflows, analyze performance and perform project actions via natural-language prompts, and it is metered via Unity Credits — this matches the story's core (scaffolding, workflow help) [unity-docs-24, unity-docs-14, unity-probe-rt-5]. However, evidence doesn't show it explicitly answering API questions or generating full scripts, there's no independent/hands-on corroboration of code-generation quality, and usage is gated behind a paid credits system rather than being freely available. Missing for 10: hands-on/community validation of the assistant's script-generation and API Q&A accuracy, explicit documentation of script-writing capability, and clarity on credit-cost limitations for heavy AI-native use.
